working: Constant Contact is authorized again after the 401 that blocked the last several runs: 100 campaigns pulled, 313,033 total sends, avg open 51.21% and avg click 1.89%.
Open rates are far above the 25-35% health/nonprofit benchmark. The Alumni list is the strongest performer: 57.30% open on the July 9 send and 55.81% on the May 27 send.

The 3-touch Alumni August sequence built toward its best click of the series: the Aug 19 'Day Of' send hit 1.84% click and 4.12% click-to-open, more than double the 0.88% click on the July 9 Alumni send.
Organic Search remains a healthy #2 channel at 10,797 sessions (33.1% of 32,585 over the 1,100-day window) and added the most sessions of any channel since the Aug 24 run (+20).

Event-driven content is the most reliable click driver on record: '2025 Alumni Events August' pulled 3.33% click on a 63.59% open, and '2025 Alumni Events September 2' pulled 2.61% click on 60.11% open.
not_working: Severe UTM leakage. Across all 91 sends in the window, GA4 credits only 15 Email sessions in the 3-day post-send windows versus 6,079 Direct sessions. Email is 21 sessions total (0.1%) against 313,033 emails delivered, while Direct sits at 16,711 (51.3%). Newsletter links carry no UTM tags, so GA4 mis-attributes essentially all newsletter traffic to Direct.

The Aug 16 'Alumni eNews - Reminder: August 2026' lift of +686% (477 sessions that day vs a 23.5 baseline, 513 Direct in 3 days) is not credible as newsletter traffic: 1,038 sends at 1.16% click is roughly 12 clicks. Treat this as a traffic anomaly or bot event, not a marketing win, and exclude it before quoting lift numbers to Todd.

Click rate is the weak half of email performance: 1.89% average against 51.21% opens. Recent Staff-Client sends are worse, at 0.43% (July 20) and 0.81% (July 2 and May 19), meaning the largest list (8,900-9,700 sends) generates the fewest clicks per open.
The Referring Partners list badly underperforms: 27.66% open on July 20 and 26.49% on June 29, roughly half the Alumni open rate and at the bottom of the benchmark band.

Several sends landed at or below flat lift: Staff-Client July 20 at -27.3%, Staff-Client July 2 at -25.3%, Alumni July 16 at +1.5%. Organic Social is thin at 1,718 sessions (5.3%) and Paid Search at 925 (2.8%).
do_next: Fix UTM tagging first, before any other optimization. Append utm_source=constantcontact&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=<send-name> to every link in the Constant Contact templates. Until this ships, no newsletter attribution number in this dashboard is trustworthy, and Email will keep reading as 0.1% of traffic.
Keep the 3-touch Alumni cadence (announce / reminder / day-of) and lead with the day-of touch: it produced the highest click and click-to-open of the August series (1.84% / 4.12%).

Repromote event content. The two strongest click performers on file are both Alumni Events sends (3.33% and 2.61% click). Build the next Staff-Client send around a dated event or deadline rather than a general update to lift its 0.43-0.81% click rate.

Rebuild the Referring Partners send: new subject-line approach and a single clear CTA. Its 4.35% click-to-open on June 29 shows the people who do open are engaged, so the problem is the open, not the offer.

Investigate the Aug 16 Direct spike (477 sessions vs ~25 baseline) in GA4 by landing page and geography, and add a bot/anomaly filter to the lift calculation so a single day cannot dominate the newsletter leaderboard.

Re-check GSC on a matched window before acting on rankings: this run's GSC pull covers only 7 days (Aug 19-26, 6 clicks, 1,395 impressions, avg position 25.95) versus a 30-day window last run (58 clicks, 4,382 impressions, avg position 14.4). The apparent slide is a window artifact, not a confirmed drop.
summary: Constant Contact reconnected this run, confirming very strong opens (51.21% avg) but weak clicks (1.89%) and near-total UTM leakage: 15 Email sessions versus 6,079 Direct across 91 sends. Adding utm_source/utm_medium tags to newsletter links is the single highest-value fix, and the Aug 16 +686% lift should be treated as a traffic anomaly rather than a newsletter win.
